parameters: You and three of your close friends exit your backyard
camping tent and enter the hot sweltering weather that all
four of you find pleasant, being natives of this tropical
island where it is hot and sometimes humid year-round.
This island where you were born and raised so far is called
"S'mee'aliere Island" and is a part of Kingdom Corr.  The
name of your home island has three syllables, and then the
word "Island."
"S'mee" is like "smee" and rhymes with "free", and the
first part of "aliere" is like "Al" which is short for
"Albert," and the last syllable is said like "leer" which
rhymes with "fear."
The stress goes on the first and third syllables.  It's a
weird name, but it isn't like you or your family named the
island or anything.
While the islands and the mainland have a strong fishing
industry, the biggest and most powerful business of all for
the Kingdom of Corr is tourism and being a desired place
for an island paradise vacation year-round.
Monsters and bandits, as well as pirates, roam the areas
between towns, and sometimes raid the towns, yet Corr is
such a treasured vacation spot that the tourism industry
thrives anyways and overcomes this issue.
Residents of Corr are known to grow up being good warriors
and combat mages and so on, and even as children wield
weapons that can kill and are not for sport.
Corr is also known for it's people being friendly and
welcoming to visitors and people on vacation.  Children
are taught at a young age to go out of their way to be nice
to visitors as well as helpful.
Your own parents are no exception.  If you were to dare
make fun of a visitor or tourist close enough that they
could hear you then your parents would smack you.....
HARD, and you wouldn't forget it.
Back to what the kingdom features, it has mountains and
grasslands of sorts as well as sand, desert, and palm trees,
and while the mountains and some of the trees have a look
of temperate climate, it's all actually very hot, all year.
When it rains, it rains warm usually, and only sometimes
cool, but never freezing cold here.  It is often humid,
and sometimes wet in some areas, while dry in others.
Stepping away from the backyard tent, the magical Book of
Destiny awaits inside.
You hear your mother calling them from inside the house.
A
Citizen: If someone joins your party as a temporary fifth
member, and is a grown-up and not a kid like you four, don't
be surprised if they are a much higher level than you and
have additional skills, as well as being better at fighting.
Kid: This game works best with a controller that has buttons
for A, B, X, Y, a D-pad, and LB and RB buttons.  If you need
to use a keyboard, try ESC and SPACE along with cursor keys.
F4 toggles full-screen.  F5 reloads the game.
Also, we don't talk about the game much outside this island!
...And plenty in this town talk about other stuff, such as
nearby dungeons and stuff you need for quests, and so on!
Citizen: Guarding with a weapon in combat is better than
using the general "guard" command.  Not all weapons offer
their own version of guarding to block incoming attacks.
Any special bonuses from guarding are temporary.
Tourist:  This town has an amazing marketplace with all
these stores!  See that shop next to the diner?  Next to
the Inn?  That's a magic shop with lots of spellbooks so
that spellcasters can actually cast spells, and they also
sell some nifty magic blasting rings!  Those rings are good
for an occasional rare blast of something in battle, and
also helpful when certain enemies are resistant to some
elements.
\P[1]: I know.  I live here, but thanks.
Tourist: You four are from here?  I'm having a lot of fun
visiting this island, and really enjoy that pub right over
there.  You're lucky to live in a town where you have stuff
like that right in town.
I can only imagine being a kid from a town like this, and
after school and during weekends just walking over to places
like that pub that are right there.  I'm here on vacation
to see things you four can enjoy any time you want!
Citizen: Ah, good to see the town guard's office is still
standing, mighty and proud, right by the entrance to the
town to keep out riff-raff.  Speaking of which, monsters
and bandits etc have been nasty lately.
The town guard is known for it's "sword and shield" but
still won't usually venture outside the town.
Where are you four off to?
Kid: Whips don't do much damage to bad guys, but are useful
to entangle them so they can't attack or do anything.
Kid: There's the town's Inn over there.  If you're going to
go out and fight monsters, you need to learn the difference
between Inns, diners, and pubs, and what they offer.
Inns and diners offer ways to heal HP based upon how much
healing you need.  Getting food at a restaurant heals only
HP (Hit Points) and no MP (Magic Points).  Staying at an
Inn recovers both.  A restaurant is less expensive.
A pub offers magic milkshakes for a flat rate that always
recovers the same, flat amount of both HP and MP to the
entire party.  This can be less expensive or wasteful.  It
depends.
Restaurants and pubs both allow chit-chat with other people
there, who are often open to conversation.
Finally, the pubs are part of a chain, so they tend to
all look the same.  Restaurants vary.  The pubs are known
for places to have a good time and many tourists visit towns
and cities for their pubs.
Kid: Living in this town, you've gotta get used to tourists
and be nice to them.  They say the towns on this island
depend on it.  I just hate it when they ask REALLY dumb
questions and are totally clueless...
The other day some lady from east of the mainland pointed
to the pub's sign outside and asked, "Is this the pub?"
I was gonna tell her "Well gee lady, why would they have
that sign there?  Hello?" but my dad would have smacked me.
Citizen: Some weapons have special attacks and other actions
specific for that type of weapon.  A club, for example, has
special blocking (guard) and attack actions, and guarding
with the weapon is better than guarding in general.
More special actions for certain weapons come as you level
up, although for some weapon types this comes faster than
others.  Simple, cheap weapons like daggers and clubs have
more actions available at lower levels.
Swords, which are top-notch, get special actions very slowly
as you level up, so at lower levels you might not have many
special actions with swords.  When your level gets higher
and you get a message about your level going up, you will
also get notifications that you've learned new special
actions that work with certain weapons, though many of them
are not for the weapon your character has equpped at the
time.
Citizen: This small diner is fast-food, with no place to
sit down to eat inside.  It's still a nice place with food
that will keep you healthy though, unlike many fast food
places.  It's not the only place in town to eat, though.
By the way, there's a weapon store in town that has it's
own built-in dining and eating area.  Kinda nifty, you
should see it.
Citizen: Jovials are masters of smoke-and-mirrors, and flashy
bright colors and illusions that confuse and charm people to
their amusement.  They are slime.  They are also poor fighters
and a decent warrior can cut them down in one strike.
Citizen: Guarding in combat is an easy way to build up
"SP", or "Special Points."
